# D75 rating validation: protocol draft, no study executed

Status: awaiting exact-hash root and independent review before code execution on study fits or outcomes. This document proposes the complete sampling and analysis procedure. Work is confined to this new directory. The original set42 calibration, failed exact-equality rule, normative fight corpus, runtime, current D65 and historical reports stay byte-identical.

D75 retains incumbent D65 and rescinds the exact-rounded-equality acceptance rule prospectively. It requires a refit improvement whose paired bootstrap interval excludes zero across prime, aging and XP-varied populations, including close pairs. Incumbent wins ties and inconclusive comparisons. Neither study below authorizes replacing D65, choosing new coefficients, changing combat, or passing remaining engineering/D74 gates.

## 1. Inputs and numerical independence

`original-input-pins.json` pins the existing independent Python engine, original 4,000 training/2,000 held-out split, archived outcomes, Decimal fit and original failure. All derivation uses the frozen Python model contract `abb5b54edd921855b81dc5b99ef29b2ac94cadc9296dcd2981af4b57ad25040f`. No new Go source or output supplies an expectation. Old held-out outcomes are historical evidence, never part of the fresh population study.

Before either study executes: copy/pin this final protocol; pin every runner/helper source, compiler/version/flags, immutable input and output schema; freeze coefficient resample indices and the complete new population input archive. Only then start refits or new fights. Input generation may validate canonical DNA/manifest/condition and integer selection rules; it must not invoke the fight model. Outcomes cannot select cases, coefficients, thresholds, labels or report strata. Preserve every failed/interrupted attempt separately.

### Available local tools and accelerator proposal

Probes found CPython3.14.3 and3.9.6, neither with NumPy installed. Apple clang/clang++21.0.0 is available for arm64. No package installation or network dependency is proposed. The hardware sysctl query was denied; this does not affect the fixed one-thread execution policy.

Use a small separately authored C++17 **statistics-only** binary64 accelerator for repeated logistic fits. It does not implement the fight engine. Compile with `-O2 -std=c++17 -ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math -fno-associative-math`; one thread, explicit scalar dot and gradient left folds, no BLAS, FMA, fused update, SIMD reduction, early stopping, regularization or reassociation. Pin source, compiler executable/version, command and binary. Every fit uses precisely 400 full-batch iterations, learning rate0.5, initial zero weights, five features in Power/Speed/Chin/Stamina/Skill order, and the existing sigmoid/clamp. Features are integer league-tenths differences divided by500. Original draw labels remain0/0.5/1. Gradients are divided by4,000 before updates. This is an explicitly validated floating approximation to the original Decimal50 procedure, not a claim of bit-identical Decimal execution for all1,000 fits.

Accuracy checks are fixed before output: reproduce the original unresampled Decimal50 fit, and recompute bootstrap replicas0,1,2,127,499,998,999 with the unchanged Decimal50/round-half-even procedure and same resampled row order. Absolute error of every raw and mean-normalized coefficient must be≤1e-8; all rounded tenth tuples must agree. Any violation stops the study; no report may silently loosen tolerance. Additionally, if the absolute accelerated raw mean is≤1e-6, any raw/normalized coefficient is nonfinite or within1e-6 of zero, or any normalized coefficient is within1e-6 of a half-tenth boundary (k/10+0.05), recompute that entire replicate with Decimal50 and use those Decimal coefficients for its statistics/frequency/validity. Nonfinite accelerator arithmetic is a validation failure if the Decimal calculation is finite; it cannot silently become a statistical invalid-fit observation. More than64 such additional replicas stops with an unresolved numerical-resource condition, preserving results for review. Report all comparisons, maximum discrepancies and fallback IDs. Do not classify a rounded tuple from an unchecked near-boundary double. At most two independent Decimal checks may execute concurrently; all output ordering is by fixed replica ID.

## 2. Study A: coefficient stability, 1,000 genuine refits

This is a training-pair bootstrap, distinct from the old fixed-predictor held-out accuracy bootstrap. Its target is uncertainty conditional on this frozen training design/model, not universal or causal attribute importance.

Use only the original4,000 training rows: five classes in order light,welter,middle,light_heavy,heavy,800 rows per class in original index order. For each replica0..999, independently draw800 training pair indices with replacement inside each class. Preserve each pair's complete features and outcome together. Feed the4,000 selected rows in class order then draw order to the original400-iteration fitting procedure; do not aggregate multiplicities or change reduction order. Repeated selected rows are deliberate bootstrap duplicates, not new fight outcomes. No simulation occurs in this study.

Exact resampling stream: key = SHA256(ASCII `SLUG D75 coefficient bootstrap\0v1\0`, actual NULs). For replica r/class c/raw counter j, word = first8 bytes, big-endian unsigned, of SHA256(key || LE32(r) || LE32(c) || LE64(j)); each replica/class counter starts0. Uniform(800) uses rejection threshold2^64 mod800, accepts word≥threshold then word mod800; at most256 words per selection and10,000,000 total raw words. Archive every selected index as little-endian uint16 absolute training-row index, exactly1,000×4,000×2 bytes, plus hashes and stream counts. Freeze before refitting.

For each replica retain raw coefficients, arithmetic mean, mean-normalized coefficients, exact rounded-tenth tuple, validity and numerical-check/fallback status. Mean≤0 or nonfinite coefficients are invalid; retain the failure and raw values, never reroll. Nonpositive individual normalized coefficients also flag invalid fit but remain visible in distributions. Do not silently discard them. If any replicate has mean≤0 or nonfinite arithmetic making normalization undefined, normalized intervals/covariance/correlations are unavailable (JSON null), with all failure counts/rows retained; do not drop rows and reuse fixed quantile indices on a smaller set. Raw summaries are likewise unavailable if any raw vector is nonfinite. Zero-variance correlation entries are unavailable (JSON null), never NaN or silently omitted. Nonpositive individual normalized coefficients with positive finite mean remain in all normalized summaries as stated.

Publish all1,000 rows; raw and normalized covariance matrices (unbiased n−1, Decimal50 accumulation over the retained decimal representations); medians and percentile intervals with sorted elements24 and974; correlations; rounded-tuple frequency table; per-coefficient rounding-boundary crossings; invalid-fit counts; and numerical accuracy evidence. Report the most common tuple without selecting it as a replacement. Normalize **each whole replicate before** taking intervals/covariance; never normalize marginal interval endpoints.

For coefficient comparisons, put incumbent D65 on the same mean-one scale: divide [1.0,2.5,0.2,0.4,0.8] by0.98. This normalization is reporting-only. Actual D65 scores/predictions and display semantics remain untouched. Also show the original continuous normalized fit and historical exact-rounded tuple frequencies, clearly labelled. No positivity/significance/stability threshold is invented to authorize a rating change.

## 3. Study B: fresh population coverage, 20,000 unique pair families

Freeze a disjoint namespace and all inputs before outcomes. All fighters are canonical independent manifests, same immutable class; one fight per unique pair family and unique bout seed. No reused fighter identity across families, repeated lifecycle versions of a pair, or repeated-seed pseudo-replication. SHA collisions/duplicate identities or InputIDs are fatal, not repaired by reroll.

Four populations explicitly cross age and XP:

| Population label | Age | Permanent XP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prime-xp0` | both age0 | both0 |
| `mixed-age-xp0` | independently assigned prime/early/mid/late positions | both0 |
| `prime-xpvar` | both age0 | ordered pair0..15 within a fixed XP-gap stratum |
| `mixed-age-xpvar` | independently assigned prime/early/mid/late positions | ordered pair0..15 within a fixed XP-gap stratum, independently assigned before phenotype rejection |

Training is0 throughout. Random fight form remains the frozen engine's normal seeded form. The mixed-age positions per original corner are prime(age0), early(elapsed decline floor(D/4)), mid(floor(D/2)), and late(D−1), with each declining age equal to that fighter's PrimeWeeks plus elapsed decline. All16 ordered age pairs occur;15/16 contain at least one declining fighter, including prime-versus-declined asymmetry. All these fighters remain pre-retirement. The original160 retired endpoint diagnostics stay separate historical evidence; this study does not claim fresh retired-population validation or change eligibility. Set common AsOfMS=1800000000000 and BornAtMS=AsOfMS−AgeWeeks×604800000. The original-corner phase and XP schedules are fixed before phenotype rejection and travel with the complete fighter when canonical IDs sort the pair.

Each population has three **separately reported** panels: natural2,000 and close2,000 (400 per class), plus D52-edge1,000 (200 per class) in the five-class order. Total4×5,000=20,000. These are balanced research cohorts, not estimates of natural user/class prevalence.

- `natural`: full same-class pair distribution; **no D52 eligibility, rating-closeness or outcome filter**. It is not advertised as the eventual matchmaker distribution.
- `close`: incumbent current D65 ratio maxRating/minRating≤1.05 (inclusive). This is a frozen research definition of close, not a new game rule.
- `d52-edge`: per class100 inside-edge cases with ratio in[1.8,2.0], and100 outside-edge cases with ratio in(2.0,2.2]. This stresses both sides of the initial D52 two-to-one band. It makes no claim about widening until five opponents, pools, matchmaking implementation or weight-class/talent-budget boundary behavior.

Selection uses exact incumbent `rating_hundredths` on aged attributes plus permanent XP, excluding form/training. Use integer comparisons: close20×max≤21×min; inside9×min≤5×max and max≤2×min; outside max>2×min and5×max≤11×min. Rates are positive for every canonical valid input. Never use rounded-refit/continuous ratings or outcomes to choose a panel. Natural and deliberately conditioned close/edge panels are never pooled into one headline accuracy.

### Exact quotas, independent schedules and generation

Define each population/class/panel unit as400 rows for natural/close, or each100-row edge side. Freeze exact design-cell counts before sampling phenotypes:

- prime-XP0: one cell per unit.
- mixed-age-XP0: the16 ordered age-position cells,25 each for400; for100, cells0..3 have7 and4..15 have6 (age-pair code4×A_position+B_position).
- prime-XP-varied: four absolute XP-gap cells0,1..5,6..10,11..15,100 each for400 or25 each for100.
- mixed-age-XP-varied:16 age-pair×4 XP-gap cells. For400, every cell has6 plus one extra when gap_code=age_pair_code mod4: each age-pair total25 and each gap total100. For100, every cell has1; add one in gap columns r mod4 and(r+1)mod4 for every age-pair r; for r=0..3 add a third at(r+2)mod4. Each gap total25; age-pairs0..3 total7 and others6.

Expand and independently shuffle these cell labels within each unit. For XP-varied rows, enumerate all ordered integer pairs(xa,xb) with0≤xa,xb≤15 whose absolute gap lies in that row's fixed gap category; choose one uniformly using a separate domain stream. This assignment happens before any phenotype/panel rejection. It covers the full XP range, including unequal levels and both orientations, without coupling XP to one age-progress index. Report every realized XP level, ordered pair and age×XP cross-tab, including absent fine cells. Gap-balanced sampling is an explicit research target, not uniform independent XP levels or natural player prevalence. No exact16×16 XP-pair marginal quota is claimed.

The fixed resampling cells are class×age-pair×XP-gap, omitting unused dimensions; edge also includes side. Primary mixed-age/XP cells contain6 or7 unique families; this is coarse empirical support, not a high-resolution coefficient/fairness claim. Edge cells contain1 or2; their intervals are explicitly descriptive/unstable, and no edge superiority conclusion follows from an artificially narrow or degenerate within-cell bootstrap. Preserve these counts and limitations rather than silently using a different sampling estimand.

All deterministic stream words are first8 SHA256 bytes interpreted big-endian. Variable ASCII labels use LE32 byte-length followed by exact ASCII. All integers below are LE32 except raw counters LE64. The unit label is `<population>/<panel>/<class>` for natural/close and `<population>/d52-edge/<class>/<inside|outside>` for edge. Define:

- Schedule key = SHA256(`SLUG D75 coverage schedule\0v1\0` || framed(unit label) || framed(`design`|`xp-pair`)). For each schedule stream, raw word j is the big-endian first8 bytes of SHA256(key || LE64(j)), counter starting0. The `design` stream shuffles the expanded cell labels by Fisher–Yates, i=n−1 down to1 selecting Uniform(i+1). The independent `xp-pair` stream selects from each row's lexicographically enumerated compatible XP pairs. Both use the same unsigned rejection algorithm,≤256 words/selection.
- For row i/pair-attempt p/original corner c/class-attempt a, manifest seed = SHA256(`SLUG D75 coverage manifest\0v1\0` || framed(unit label) || LE32(i)||LE32(p)||LE32(c)||LE32(a)). Pick the first a yielding the required class. Both corner class-attempt streams start0 for each p. Project scheduled age/XP, test only the frozen panel rating rule, and accept the first matching whole pair p. A failed pair discards both candidate manifests; it never changes scheduled phase/XP.
- ProspectID = SHA256(`SLUG D75 coverage identity\0v1\0` || raw32(manifest seed) || framed(unit label) || LE32(i)||LE32(c)). Distinct IDs do not claim admitted fighters.
- Bout seed = SHA256(`SLUG D75 coverage bout\0v1\0` || framed(unit label) || LE32(i)). It is independent of rejected attempts and never chosen from outcomes.

Each class search and whole-pair search allows at most4,096 attempts; total manifest derivations across the whole construction are capped at2,000,000. Schedule draws cap at1,000,000 raw words. Exhaustion stops before outcomes and preserves the partial input attempt; no silent cap/definition/count relaxation. Any revision requires a new reviewed protocol/input freeze. Record all accepted attempt indices, quota schedules and total rejection counts. Store common observation, complete input, condition projections, panel/class/population, age/XP assignments before and after canonical sorting, D65 ratings, ratio numerator/denominator and InputID. Freeze exact archive and source hashes before invoking the engine.

Run the unchanged independent Python integer engine exactly once per input. Save the full result, digest, all draw/finish/bounds checks and labels. Also run the immutable original-source simulator on each identical input using the already documented adapter and CPython3.14.3: canonical identities/manifests, aged base attributes, XP plus training once, exact unchanged seed, title=false/featured=false. Pin simulator SHA37ff08917ed720e3d9c4f3b14508c57b08d830f9f4cb01833fa412dbca9b6422 and reuse the reviewed adapter, never its fighter generator. Archive its winner, method, last-entered round and scores. This baseline retains its original floats/RNG/draw margin and is a separate numerical outcome series, not a normative parity oracle. No engine fitting or game change occurs. The old normative corpus remains the code-conformance oracle. Any invalid state/stream/cancellation/write failure is retained and prevents a complete study report; no outcomes are silently omitted.

### Fixed predictors, paired resampling and reporting

Predictors are fixed in advance: incumbent D65 [1.0,2.5,0.2,0.4,0.8], original rounded challenger[0.9,2.5,0.2,0.6,0.8], and original full-precision continuous fit from the pinned `fit.json`. Coefficient-bootstrap output cannot replace or optimize these predictors. Continuous is a benchmark, not an automatically selectable alternative. Score draws first at0.5; rating ties0.5; otherwise correct favourite1/incorrect0. Retain exact half-point totals and paired per-family score differences; normalized coefficient scale does not alter the incumbent's actual computation.

Use10,000 paired bootstrap replicas per panel, resampling pair families with replacement within every fixed design cell defined above, drawing exactly its original family count; class/age-pair/XP-gap quotas and edge side are therefore preserved. Singleton cells reproduce their one observed family and must be counted as such, not advertised as evidence of zero underlying uncertainty. The same selected rows are used for all predictors/differences and paired engine-versus-source outcome summaries. Key = SHA256(`SLUG D75 population bootstrap\0v1\0` || framed(population/panel)). For replica r/stratum s/counter j, SHA256(key||LE32(r)||LE32(s)||LE64(j)) produces the word. The fixed population order is prime-xp0,mixed-age-xp0,prime-xpvar,mixed-age-xpvar and panel order natural,close,d52-edge. Within a panel, assign zero-based stratum IDs lexicographically by class order(light,welter,middle,light_heavy,heavy), edge side(inside,outside) if applicable, age-pair code0..15 if applicable, then XP-gap code0..3 if applicable; omitted dimensions are ignored. Within each cell, row order is its original ascending unit-row index i, never sorted by outcomes or final fighter ID. Counters reset per replica/stratum; Uniform uses the same bounded rejection. Global resampling cap250,000,000 words. All replica half-point totals and difference totals are archived. With12 panels this is200,000,000 accepted draws, before negligible rejections.

For each population/panel report ordinary two-sided95% percentile intervals: sorted replica indices249 and9749. Report paired challenger-minus-incumbent and continuous-minus-incumbent intervals; separate individual predictor intervals are not a paired-improvement test. There are eight policy-relevant natural/close comparisons across four populations. A D75-supported challenger claim requires **every one** of these eight ordinary paired intervals to have lower endpoint strictly>0. Zero, negative, invalid or incomplete is inconclusive/adverse and the incumbent stays. Never substitute a favourable aggregate or class for a failed panel. This reports evidence under the user decision; even an all-positive result does not authorize adoption.

Also report nominal simultaneous Bonferroni-adjusted percentile intervals for those eight fixed challenger comparisons using indices31 and9968 (tail probabilities0.003125 and0.996875, nearest-rank convention). Label these approximate bootstrap simultaneous diagnostics, not exact finite-sample coverage or a new undisclosed release gate. The D52-edge panels receive ordinary descriptive intervals with their explicit small/singleton-cell limitation and full diagnostics; D75 did not specify a new edge-only superiority threshold, so none is invented. Adverse edge findings remain visible for product review.

Publish each panel/class's sample count, accuracy half-points, comparison changes, mean/quantiles of fixed-predictor rating gaps, actual age fractions/phases, both XP levels and absolute XP gap bins0,1..5,6..10,11..15, rarity/talent-budget mix, physical ranges, methods/round lengths, canonical-corner outcomes and all rejection counts. Include zero-count categories and the pre-sort age/XP cross-tabs. For each population/panel also report paired new-engine versus immutable source-baseline finish fractions, draw fractions and mean integer last-entered round, with per-family paired differences and same-resample diagnostic intervals. Include the complete method tables with zeros. These are descriptive outcome-distribution checks; do not transplant original natural-prime calibration thresholds onto close or edge panels. No omitted negative class/phase result; no equality conflation with statistical equivalence.

## 4. Resources, preservation and result interpretation

No installation, network, Go source, public nodes, production resources or original-file edits. All scripts/binary/intermediate/raw results live here. Computation is serial by default; at most two independent Decimal checks may run alongside a single bounded simulation or accelerator process. Limit each accelerator/check subprocess to30minutes, input construction30minutes, simulation30minutes and population bootstrap30minutes. A timeout is recorded incomplete, never a pass or reason to change counts. Cap new retained artifacts at1GiB and require that much free space before beginning; flush bounded JSONL/gzip streams rather than retaining full transcripts in memory. Keep results sorted by frozen IDs, not completion order.

Reports distinguish: coefficient uncertainty from training refits; prediction uncertainty conditional on fixed predictors; natural versus conditioned stress populations; float approximation checks from exact engine conformance; historical failed equality from amended D75 policy; evidence from permission. A closed interval including0 is inconclusive, not proof of equality. A coefficient interval including the incumbent is likewise not a causal or fairness conclusion. Multiple observed model changes and population differences are not individually attributed by this design.

Original reports stay untouched and explicitly failed under their original rule. New reports cite D75 as a post-result policy amendment, not retroactive success. No new model tuning or predictor selection uses these fresh outcomes. A future outcome-informed change needs a new prospective contract/namespace. D65 remains compiled/published throughout and after these studies unless separately authorized.
